adjacent_skills.you_have: STM32 bare-metal firmware + closed-loop feedback control

key_responsibilities: Analyze software requirements and develop verification criteria
Configure and build embedded software, including design, development and validation of software flash files for application teams
Create, execute and document test plans
Set up and configure test bench hardware and software
Complete mandatory and feature-specific testing using manual and automated methods
Troubleshoot software and system defects and provide customer support

strengths: Bench setup and hardware-level defect triage is genuinely strong: 'Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture)' in COFFIN is exactly the troubleshoot-defects-and-support-application-teams responsibility, and the Tools list carries oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, spectrum analyzers.

Embedded C at register level is real, not a keyword: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor programs GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1 directly, with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and an interrupt-driven low-level I2C driver at 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM and a deterministic 1 Hz rate.

Closed-loop control implemented from first principles: Robocon derives heading from dual-axis quadrature encoder odometry (2400 CPR) and feeds angular error back into rotation PWM at 15 kHz, plus a 4-bit A/B transition state machine on hardware interrupts and a fail-safe state machine halting motors on controller disconnect.

Verification discipline with golden references, which is the closest thing in the profile to 'develop verification criteria': QAT exported 100 golden test vectors and a pure-integer reference model, matching the float reference on 99.996% of hidden values at identical test accuracy.
Embedded OS experience is backed at working depth: Object Tracking Turret runs FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination alongside interrupt-driven UART and multi-servo PWM.

Automated test and benchmark harness construction recurs across the profile (HellaSwag/GSM8K/ARC evaluation, pynvml/psutil profiling, four MPI work-distribution strategies benchmarked head to head), which maps onto 'manual and automated methods' testing.
real_gaps: Model-Based Development, MATLAB, Simulink and Stateflow appear nowhere in the profile. MBD is a REQUIRED qualification here and it is the toolchain the application and library team works in daily; the role's build-and-validate-flash-files work is generated from models.
CAN and SAE J1939 have no backing at any depth. Serial work is UART/I2C/SPI only; no bus arbitration, no DBC/J1939 PGN-SPN work, no CAN tooling (CANoe, CANalyzer, Busmaster).

No engine, powertrain, machine or vehicle controls domain exposure. Nothing in the profile touches diesel, battery-electric or fuel-cell systems, so the entire product context would be learned from zero.

Formal software requirements analysis and traceable verification criteria are unevidenced. The profile shows ad-hoc validation against physical outcomes (10/10 pick trials, <2mm repeatability) rather than requirements-driven V-model verification with documented criteria.

'Develop embedded software library activities' has no analogue. Every firmware artifact in the profile is a single-purpose application; there is no reusable library owned across multiple consuming application teams, and no configuration management of software variants at product-line scale.

Flash-file configuration and build at production scale is unevidenced. He flashes his own MCU images and uses CMake, but there is no evidence of building, versioning and releasing calibration/variant flash files as a deliverable handed to downstream application teams.

Seniority, noted as prose and deliberately not scored here: 0 years full-time against a 5+ year requirement, and the posting describes a contributor already fluent in an established toolchain rather than someone being trained into it.

No named debugger or debug-probe experience. Debugging depth is real but is logic-analyzer/oscilloscope/Proteus-shaped; no bullet names JTAG, SWD, GDB, Trace32, Lauterbach or an ECU calibration tool such as ETAS INCA or Vector CANape.
overstated_by_keywords: Ethernet — scored Have via a generic 'networking' canonical, but the evidence is application-layer and Linux-admin: WebSocket fabric, Flask-SocketIO, static IP configuration and systemd service networking. There is no embedded Ethernet stack work (lwIP, raw sockets on an MCU, switched in-vehicle Ethernet), which is what an engine-controls posting means by the term.

Debuggers / debugging & troubleshooting — scored Have at 'strong' depth through aliases including JTAG and GDB, but no profile bullet actually names a debugger or debug probe. The underlying skill is hardware bring-up and bench triage, which is adjacent but not the same claim.

Software flash files — counted Adjacent via 'MCU firmware flashing', which understates the distance. The JD means designing and validating release flash images for other teams to consume, a configuration-management activity, not programming your own board.

Test plan creation & verification criteria — scored Have via a broad 'testing and validation' canonical. He executes and documents validation, but 'analyze software requirements and develop verification criteria' is the upstream half, and that half has no backing.
understated_by_keywords: Embedded control software development was only counted Adjacent, yet the Robocon project is a complete closed-loop controller built from scratch — error derivation from encoder odometry, feedback into PWM, interrupt-driven quadrature decoding as a state machine, and angle-weighted joystick-to-wheel mixing derived from atan2 to kill PWM saturation at 45 degrees. For a controls role this is stronger than Adjacent.

Requirements-to-verification thinking is better evidenced than any keyword suggested, through the QAT golden-vector flow: a pure-integer reference implementation plus 100 exported golden vectors used as the pass/fail criterion. That is bit-exact regression methodology, which is how flash-file validation is actually judged.

Systems-integration troubleshooting across a multi-team boundary never string-matched anything, but 'customer support for system and software issues' is precisely what the COFFIN three-layer pipeline work and the ARC role (owning wiring, interfacing and integration across mechanical and design teams) demonstrate.

Hands-on electrical troubleshooting is undersold by a single keyword hit: custom single-layer PCB design and fabrication in EAGLE, sensor comms over UART/I2C with closed-loop feedback, and diagnosing a servo brown-out are real electrical-system fault-finding.
screening_gaps: Zero Model-Based Development / Simulink / Stateflow — it is listed under REQUIRED qualifications, not preferred, and it is the medium the application and library team actually works in. A screener filters on this term first and the profile cannot answer it at any depth.

Zero years professional industry experience against an explicit 5+ year requirement, with no production engine or machine controls work to offset it. Seven internships and a capstone do not read as five years of shipped controls software to a recruiter screening for a Fortune 100 client site.

No CAN or SAE J1939 at all — this is the bus every ECU on a diesel and electrified off-highway product line speaks, and it is absent even at hobby level in the profile, so bench and integration tasks would start from zero on day one.
llm_analysis.reasoning: The bench-and-integration half of this job is genuinely backed — register-level embedded C, closed-loop control written from first principles, FreeRTOS with mutexes, golden-vector regression validation, and a specific, credible defect-triage narrative. The other half is not: Model-Based Development is a required qualification with zero evidence, and MATLAB/Simulink/Stateflow, CAN/J1939 and the entire engine/electrified-powertrain domain are all absent, which is also why the keyword and semantic reads land within three points of each other instead of the usual wide gap. Against a 5+ year requirement at a staffing firm placing into a Fortune 100 client site with sponsorship unstated, this does not survive a screen on its own merits.
